findings.title: Remounted controlled control no longer resets stale filled state
findings.suggested_fix: In the mount-time layout effect, set filled from the DOM both ways: setFilled(Boolean(validation.inputRef.current?.value)). This keeps the 'does not set filled state on mount for an empty controlled value' test passing. Assumes one Field.Control per Field.Root.

residual_risks: Post-submit reset now surfaces required errors: submitAttemptedRef and markedDirtyRef are never reset, so resetting a required controlled Field.Control to '' after a submit (for example in onFormSubmit) now runs validation.change('') and shows valueMissing. Base left the field valid. A scratch test confirmed this, and Checkbox.Root does the same on head, so this is intentional sibling parity rather than a defect, but it changes what users see after a text-input reset.

In controlled mode the React #9023 defaultPrevented workaround no longer applies. If the input event is prevented but the consumer still accepts the value, the field clears errors and validates (1 call on head vs 0 on base). This looks correct because the value did change, but the existing 'change is prevented' test covers only uncontrolled mode.
testing_gaps: No test covers the PR's claim that a controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites never reaches field state (a rejected edit should keep the server error and skip validate; an uppercasing consumer should have validate receive the rewritten value).
No test covers a programmatic controlled change superseding a pending async validator for the old value.

findings.title: Rejected or rewritten controlled value contract has no test
findings.suggested_fix: Add two cases to FieldControl.test.tsx. (1) Rejected: `value="" onValueChange={() => {}}` in onChange mode; type 'a'; assert root has no data-dirty, no data-filled, and validate was not called. (2) Rewritten: `onValueChange={(v) => setValue(v.toUpperCase())}`; type 'a'; assert validate was called only with 'A'. Both pass on the reviewed head (scratch probe).

findings.title: Form error clearing on controlled value change untested
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test with a stable `const errors = { message: 'Server error' }` passed to `<Form errors={errors}>`, wrapping a controlled `<Field.Control value={v} onValueChange={setV} />` plus a button that calls setV('x'). Click the button and assert 'Server error' is gone. Optionally add a typed-change variant. Passes on the reviewed head (scratch probe).

residual_risks: When `<Form errors={{...}}>` is an inline object literal in the same component that owns the controlled value, typing does not clear the server error: Form's parent-level useValueChanged(externalErrors) runs after the child's clearErrors and re-applies the new object reference. Confirmed on the reviewed head in a scratch probe. By reading the code this also happened before the diff, but I did not run it against base. Tests for this path need a stable errors reference.
testing_gaps: No test mounts a controlled Field.Control with a non-empty `value` and checks data-filled. The diff removed the valueProp-based mount branch, so this now relies only on the DOM read in the mount layout effect. The new mount test uses uncontrolled defaultValue.

Controlled Field.Control with a prevented input event is untested. The test 'does not clear errors or validate when change is prevented' (FieldControl.test.tsx:214) covers only uncontrolled mode. In controlled mode, onChange returns early (FieldControl.tsx:144) before the defaultPrevented check for facebook/react#9023. If the consumer's onValueChange still commits the value, useValueChanged (FieldControl.tsx:105-115) runs clearErrors(name) and validation.change, so a prevented edit now clears a Form server error that the base code kept. Add a controlled variant of that test to pin down the intended contract.

findings.title: Format-on-blur wipes the onBlur validation error it just produced
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror NumberFieldInput's blockRevalidationRef: in the internal onBlur (when validationMode === 'onBlur') set a ref like blurCommitRef.current = true, and clear it in a layout effect after that commit. In the useValueChanged callback, when blurCommitRef.current && !shouldValidateOnChange(), reset the flag and call validation.commit(serializedValue) so the normalized value gets fully validated, instead of validation.change(serializedValue) and its revalidate shortcut. This assumes a value change that lands in the same batch as a blur should get the full blur-time validation.

residual_risks: Registered controlled value is now String(value). Form submit and actionsRef.validate() go through getRegistrationValue, so a Field `validate` callback on a controlled non-string value now receives '5' or 'a,b' where it used to receive 5 or ['a','b']. That makes change and submit consistent, but it is an observable contract shift for validators written against the raw type.
testing_gaps: No test covers a controlled Field.Control in validationMode='onBlur' where the value changes programmatically in the same batch as the blur (normalize-on-blur). That scenario regressed in this diff and is not exercised.

AGENTS.md Testing asks for "writing new tests where applicable". The PR says "A controlled value the consumer rejects or rewrites no longer reaches the field state": in FieldControl.tsx, onChange returns early when isControlled. FieldControl.test.tsx has no test where onValueChange ignores or rewrites the typed value and then asserts that data-dirty, data-filled and validate calls follow the committed prop value instead of the typed input.
